previous.text: The party brought hired killer Drop Dead Ned to the Barrow Mound, where he offered to buy the goblin bodies.
Sir Phidipaldi laid out a step-by-step plan to slay the dragon. Tomb mosaics showed Brandon killing it through the roof of its mouth.
Sir Phidipaldi took Sir Brandon's magic sword and plate armor from the knight's sarcophagus.
The party found goblins hacked apart below the mound. Saint Arthur's statue blessed Sir Phidipaldi for the rest of the barrow.
Claiming to be Sir Brandon's son, Sir Phidipaldi struck a bargain with the Free Goblin Society in the crypt.
Dr. Uriah donned Saint Arthur's holy robes over Brother Dirk's objections, and Trout kept the jeweled chalice.
The party answered a voice's riddle with four knightly virtues, opening stone doors beyond a noblewoman's statue.

current.where_you_are: The party is in Sir Brandon's tomb, about to leave.

immediate_danger.text: A seven-foot brown skeleton in rusted armor and a mustachioed death mask stands in the doorway, dragging a huge greatsword. The goblins say it killed many of their kin below, and the slime says it is very mad.

Your goals.text: Kill the black dragon and drag its body into Brandonsford to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold.
Find the treasure marked on the party's treasure map.
Fight Eric the Reeve in the duel Sir Phidipaldi challenged him to at dawn.

Standing in your way.text: The dragon has a deadly poison bite, and George says no arrow or sword pierces its scales. Father William says only Sir Brandon's sword can kill it.
Farmer Gill won't lower his price for Shamus until his boys come back to help with the work.
Farmer Gill says Warwick always refuses to sell the mithril chain shirt he displays.

What could help.text: Sir Phidipaldi carries Sir Brandon's magic sword, the blade that killed the first dragon.
George says the dragon's lair is north at the foot of the mountains, with no climbing needed.
Squints has joined the party as Trout's junior assistant.
The party holds a treasure map marking several unknown locations near Brandonsford.
If the party checks one of the map's locations on its way north through the forest, they can learn what it marks.
If the party pays Lady Hilda, she will join them against the dragon.
Dunk says that if the party gets Warwick's mithril chain shirt, it could help against the dragon.
If the party hires Lady Hilda, they gain a seasoned fighter for the dragon hunt.
Dunk says that if the party gets the mithril chain shirt, they will have magical armor.

Still unanswered.text: Who does the noblewoman statue with the stone sword depict?
Where has this new dragon come from?
Why has nothing reached Brandonsford in months?
Why are the once-hidden fairies coming out more often?
Whose female voice asked the party what makes a true knight?

Promises and debts.text: The party must clear the evil from the Barrow Mound so the goblins can live there free of King Hogboon. In return the goblins walk with the party and give Sir Phidipaldi his 'father's goods'.
Dunk must help Ingrid get into Warwick's house and give Warwick her sleeping potion, in return for her making it.
Trout must let Squints pick from the Halfling Corps' first treasure after the elite members. It's unclear whether the barrow's loot counts.
Sir Phidipaldi must bring his lance against the dragon, as he vowed to George.

Meanwhile.text: The black dragon that tore off George the woodsman's arm is still at large around Brandonsford and may maim others.
George says the dragon can't fly yet but soon will, and then they are doomed.
The man-eating giant in the cyclopean cottage north of Brandonsford is now awake. He chased the party until he tired.

threads.name: The dragon and the Reeve's bounty
threads.note: Sir Phidipaldi now holds Sir Brandon's magical sword (beat_54) and laid out a plan for the hunt, but the dragon is still at large and the bounty unclaimed.

threads.name: Hiring Lady Hilda
threads.note: The plan to pay Lady Hilda with an advance from the reeve adds to the hiring, which is still pending.

threads.name: Drop Dead Ned's offer
threads.note: The offer was accepted: Ned is now formally hired on new terms, paying 10 gold back per murder with the body his (beat_1), and has offered to buy the goblin bodies.

threads.name: Sir Phidipaldi's quarrel with Eric the Reeve
Warwick's mithril chain shirt
threads.note: Getting the shirt through Dunk's scheme remains a step in the party's plan; the shirt is not yet obtained.

threads.name: Squints and Trout's Halfling Corps
threads.note: Squints proved himself by killing the ooze and is acting under Trout's orders; the recruitment terms and Trout's secret intent still stand.

threads.name: Ingrid's sleeping potion for Warwick
threads.note: Dunk's potion scheme is still part of the plan and the debt to Ingrid is unfulfilled.

threads.name: Sir Brandon's magic sword at the Barrow Mound
threads.note: The sword was found in Sir Brandon's sarcophagus and taken by Sir Phidipaldi (beat_54), and Brother Dirk came along to the Barrow, so nothing about the retrieval remains open.

threads.name: Dr. Uriah's penance and donation at the Barrow Mound
threads.note: The party reached the Barrow Mound but no penance or donation was shown, so the debt stands.

threads.name: Why the hidden fairies are coming out
The giant in the cyclopean cottage
The undead swordsman of the Barrow Mound
threads.note: A huge, angry undead figure with a greatsword, possibly one of Brandon's companions, has slaughtered goblins below and has just appeared in the tomb's doorway (beat_55); the danger is live.

threads.name: The Free Goblin Society's bargain
threads.note: Sir Phidipaldi promised to clear the evil from the mound and keep the goblins hidden from King Hogboon in exchange for their company and his 'father's goods' (beat_14); the clearing is unfinished.

threads.name: Brother Dirk and the Barrow's holy relics
threads.note: Dr. Uriah wears the robes of Saint Arthur, whose magic is untested, over Dirk's offence, and whether the chalice belongs to the church was left to 'figure out later' (beat_49).

threads.name: The noblewoman statue and the voice in the tomb
threads.note: No one knows who the noblewoman statue depicts or whose voice asked the knightly riddle; the doors opened but the question stands.

facts.text: Find the treasure marked on the party's treasure map.
The party holds a treasure map marking several locations they do not recognize, near Brandonsford.

classification.support_basis: The map is the party's only guide to the treasure's possible locations, though they do not recognize the marked places.

facts.text: Where is the treasure the map marks?

classification.grounding_justification: The map marks several unrecognized locations, clearly leaving the treasure's location unresolved.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Answering it mostly supplies a location, though checking several sites is involved.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly instrumental for finding the treasure.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Checking the marked locations supports following leads across the region.

facts.text: The party plans to check one of the map's marked locations on its way north through the forest.

classification.support_basis: Checking a marked location could reveal whether the treasure lies there, using a journey the party already plans.
classification.action_basis: The party holds the map and planned the detour on its northward route, so the check is a supported physical option.

facts.text: Where did the party's treasure map come from?

classification.grounding_justification: Raised in an earlier session as an unexplained gap about the map's origin; nothing this Session adds to it.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The origin could reveal who made the map and why, a hidden circumstance.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Could be mildly interesting but is mainly background.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Little established beyond possibly asking around about the map.

facts.text: Naggeneen, held in a bag behind Quinn's bar at the Golden Egg, offers his pot of gold or a secret to whoever lets him go.

classification.support_basis: The offer of gold or a secret has no established connection to any current want or debt of the party.
classification.action_basis: Naggeneen himself offered his pot of gold or a secret in exchange for being released, though freeing him means acting behind Quinn's bar.

facts.text: What does Quinn intend to do with the captive Naggeneen?

classification.grounding_justification: Quinn holding a fairy captive in a bag behind his bar clearly raises the question of his purpose.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer reveals an intention, but likely one straightforward discovery would settle it.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mildly interesting, mainly bearing on whether to free Naggeneen.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Asking Quinn or Naggeneen would likely settle it.

facts.text: Kill the black dragon troubling Brandonsford and drag its body into town to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold.
Lady Hilda would join the party against the dragon for pay (see her offer's thread).

classification.support_basis: An extra fighter adds strength against the dragon, though she alone cannot pierce its scales.
classification.action_basis: Lady Hilda offered to join for pay; the party must pay her.

facts.text: Where has this new dragon come from, centuries after Sir Brandon killed the first?

classification.grounding_justification: A dragon reappearing centuries after the first was slain is a conspicuous anomaly.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal an underlying cause for the dragon's return.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Would explain events and could reframe the dragon threat.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be pursued through legends, the lair and locals.

facts.text: The black dragon, which tore off George the woodsman's arm, is still at large around Brandonsford and may maim others.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Maiming or killing of locals is specific.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: George's missing arm is direct evidence.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: The dragon has already attacked and remains active, but no further pattern was shown.
classification.preventability_justification: The party now holds the sword said to kill it.

facts.text: Farmer Gill's three sons are hunting the dragon now and could kill it before the party, taking the Reeve's bounty.

classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: They are hunting it, but weapons have failed against it.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: They are actively hunting, but success is unlikely given past failures.
classification.preventability_justification: The party can hurry the hunt.

facts.text: George says the dragon's lair is up north at the foot of the mountains, with no climbing needed.

classification.support_basis: Tells the party where to find the dragon.

facts.text: Nothing pierces the dragon's black scales: George says his friends' arrows and swords all failed, and Father William says it can't be killed without the magic sword buried with Sir Brandon. Its jaws drip poison whose bite kills, and it spits sulfur.

classification.scope_basis: The dragon's invulnerability and poison are inherent and remain until it is killed; obtaining the sword has not yet been tested against it.

facts.text: The magic sword buried with Sir Brandon at the Barrow Mound is said to be the only way to kill the dragon (see its thread).
facts.ended_how: used up: Sir Phidipaldi took the sword from the tomb; replaced by fact_new_1

classification.support_basis: Said to be the only weapon able to kill the dragon.
classification.action_basis: The sword lay in the Barrow Mound, which the party could reach.

facts.text: Dunk says Warwick's mithril chain shirt could help against the dragon (see its thread).

classification.support_basis: Better armor would reduce the danger of fighting the dragon.
classification.action_basis: Dunk's scheme to obtain it is part of Sir Phidipaldi's plan.

facts.text: George says the dragon can't fly yet but soon will, and then they are doomed.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: A flying dragon would be far harder to stop and could ravage the region.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: George calls it doom for the town.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: George says flight is coming soon, but no timing is given.
classification.preventability_justification: Killing the dragon soon would prevent it.

facts.text: Does Eric the Reeve actually have the 1000 gold he promised for the dragon?

classification.grounding_justification: Doubt about the reeve's funds was raised in earlier play.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A single check of the reeve's means would settle it.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi vowed to George to bring his lance against the dragon, which George allows may be one of the few weapons not yet tried.

classification.stake_basis: George wants the dragon dead but has no established interest in the lance specifically beyond allowing it might be untried.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi carries Sir Brandon's magical sword, the blade that killed the first dragon: silvery white, not cursed, etched "All shadows yield to my light".

classification.support_basis: Said to be the only weapon that can kill the dragon whose scales nothing else pierces, though it is untested against this dragon.

facts.resource_subject: Sir Brandon's magical sword, now carried by Sir Phidipaldi

facts.text: The Barrow Mound mosaics show Sir Brandon slew the first dragon by driving his sword up through the roof of its open mouth.

classification.support_basis: Suggests a proven point of attack against a dragon, though it comes from a depiction of the first dragon.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi plans to stop at the witch's place or the alchemist for protection against the black dragon's poison.

classification.support_basis: Protection would reduce the risk of the dragon's deadly poisonous bite, but neither the witch nor the alchemist is established to offer such protection.
classification.action_basis: It is the party's plan, but no witch or alchemist has been shown to have or offer poison protection.

facts.text: Lady Hilda, a seasoned fighter in chain mail with a shield, offers to join the party against the dragon for pay.

classification.support_basis: An experienced armored fighter would add real strength to the party's fight against the dragon, though her price is not yet set or funded.
classification.action_basis: Lady Hilda herself offered her services for pay; the party must return and pay her.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi told Lady Hilda the party would talk to the Reeve and then come back to take up her services.

classification.stake_basis: Lady Hilda offered paid work, but no evidence shows she relies on the party returning rather than simply being hired.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi plans to use Sir Brandon's sword as proof of competence to strong-arm the reeve into an advance, then use the advance to pay Lady Hilda and henchmen.

classification.support_basis: An advance would fund hiring Lady Hilda and henchmen for the dragon fight, though the reeve has not agreed to pay anything early.
classification.action_basis: The party now holds Sir Brandon's sword to show the reeve, but no evidence shows the reeve has agreed to an advance.

facts.resource_subject: An advance from the reeve to pay Lady Hilda

facts.text: Drop Dead Ned, a thief with a killer wasp in a jar, offers himself and the wasp for hire at 100 gold a week, doing anything as long as he gets to kill people; Dr. Uriah said he would think about it.
facts.ended_how: used up: the party formally hired Ned on new terms

classification.support_basis: A hireable killer and scout; no specific want was established that the hire served.
classification.action_basis: Ned explicitly offered his services for a stated fee.

facts.text: Drop Dead Ned, a killer with a little killer wasp, is hired by the party for a 100 gold fee and travels with them, scouting ahead and carrying tools such as a crowbar.

classification.support_basis: Ned adds a scout and killer to the party, but play has not tied him to a specific want or debt.

facts.text: Ned pays the party 10 gold back each time they let him murder somebody, provided he may do whatever he wants with the body.

classification.support_basis: A small payment per killing; no want or debt it serves is established.
classification.action_basis: Ned agreed to these terms as part of his hiring; the party must let him kill someone and keep the body.

facts.text: Ned offers to buy the bodies of the dead goblins in the Barrow Mound's lower corridor for 5 gold each.

classification.support_basis: A small sum of money; no want or debt it serves is established.
classification.action_basis: Ned explicitly offered 5 gold per body and Wayman found it fair; the party must hand over the bodies.

facts.resource_subject: Ned's offer to buy the goblin bodies and the need to sneak them past the goblins

facts.text: The Free Goblin Society would not want their dead compatriots defiled, so the party would have to sneak the goblin bodies past them to sell them to Ned.

classification.scope_basis: The goblins live in the mound and hold this value generally, so the objection lasts as long as the bodies must pass them.

facts.text: Why has nothing come into Brandonsford in months, including Bentley's restock shipment that was due a week ago?

classification.grounding_justification: A whole town receiving no shipments for months, with a specific overdue restock, is a conspicuous anomaly established in prior play.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal an underlying cause cutting off the town's supply.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Learning what is choking off Brandonsford would explain a regional situation.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Supports following trade routes, questioning merchants and travellers.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi wants to fight Eric the Reeve in the duel he challenged him to at dawn.
Will Eric the Reeve, offended by Sir Phidipaldi, accept his challenge to a duel at dawn?

classification.grounding_justification: A challenge was issued in an earlier Session and the Reeve's response was left open; nothing this Session revisits it.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer is a simple yes or no about the Reeve's response.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Knowing whether he accepts is mildly interesting but mainly sets up a confrontation.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: It would be settled by returning to the Reeve and seeing his response.

facts.text: Get Farmer Gill's mule Shamus; Gill asked 100 gold but says he is willing to go lower.
When Dunk asked to trade work for Shamus, Farmer Gill said the big work needed is killing the dragon; he did not say outright he would give the mule for it.

classification.support_basis: Killing the dragon might earn Gill's goodwill toward handing over Shamus, but Gill never agreed to give the mule for it.
classification.action_basis: Gill only named the dragon as the big work needed; he did not agree to trade the mule for it.

facts.text: Farmer Gill can get no work done without his boys or a mule, so he won't drop his price for Shamus until his boys come back.

classification.scope_basis: Gill's stated condition lasts until his boys return, which has not happened.

facts.text: Acquire the mithril chain shirt Warwick the smith displays in his shop.
Farmer Gill says Warwick always refuses to sell the mithril chain shirt he displays.

classification.scope_basis: Warwick's refusal is a standing habit, not tied to one scene, and the party has not yet visited him.

facts.text: Dunk says Warwick's mithril chain shirt is magical armor that could help against the dragon, once the party has it.

classification.support_basis: Magical armor would protect a fighter against the dragon, though its magic rests on Dunk's word and is unspecified.
classification.action_basis: The party must first obtain the shirt, which Warwick refuses to sell; the plan to get it through Dunk's scheme is part of Sir Phidipaldi's dragon plan.

facts.text: Dunk's plan to help Ingrid get her sleeping potion to Warwick could let him into Warwick's house to take the shirt.

classification.support_basis: It offers a way around Warwick's refusal to sell by getting into his house while he sleeps, though success is untested.
classification.action_basis: Dunk proposed the scheme and Sir Phidipaldi's plan includes returning to carry it out to get the shirt.

facts.text: What magic does Warwick's mithril chain shirt hold?

classification.grounding_justification: Dunk called the shirt magical without saying what it does, which raises the question.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Identifying an item's property is a simple fact.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly instrumental information about the armor.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Likely settled by examining the shirt or a magic test such as Ingrid's powder.

facts.text: Under Trout's recruitment terms, once the Halfling Corps finds its first treasure Squints gets to pick from it after the elite members; until then Squints funds himself and his gear and takes orders from Trout.
facts.uncertain_reason: The party took treasure in the Barrow Mound this Session (some fetched on Squints's orders), but play never said whether that counts as the Corps' first treasure or whether Squints has picked yet.

classification.stake_basis: Squints accepted self-funding and taking orders specifically in exchange for a pick of the first treasure.

facts.text: Squints, a halfling more experienced at fighting than Trout and armed with a sling and dagger, has joined the party as Trout's junior assistant and takes orders directly from Trout.

classification.support_basis: Squints adds a capable sling fighter under Trout's command, as shown when he killed the gray ooze, a small added strength for the party's dangerous pursuits.

facts.text: Trout, with Phidipaldi's agreement, secretly intends not to rescue Squints if he is caught while sent into danger, despite promising him intervention.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: The specific harm is Squints being left captured or killed in danger without the promised rescue.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Serious harm or death to one henchman and a broken trust.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: The intent was stated by Trout and agreed by Phidipaldi.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Trout keeps sending Squints on tasks in a dangerous dungeon, but he has not yet been caught.
classification.preventability_justification: The party controls the decision and can choose to rescue Squints or not send him into danger.

facts.text: Dunk owes Ingrid help getting into Warwick's house and giving Warwick her sleeping potion, so she can watch him sleep without fear of waking him, in exchange for her making the potion.

classification.stake_basis: Ingrid made the potion on these terms because she specifically wants to watch Warwick sleep without fear of waking him.

facts.text: Ingrid is making a sleeping potion from the faun wine Dunk gave her; Dunk can collect it when they meet tonight and use it to put Warwick to sleep.

classification.support_basis: Putting Warwick to sleep lets the party take the mithril chain shirt without him waking, though it is unclear whether the diluted wine makes a working potion.
classification.action_basis: Ingrid agreed to make the potion for Dunk to collect, and the party's plan is to carry out Dunk's scheme to get the chain shirt.

facts.text: Warwick sleeps in a second-story bedroom above his shop whose window is left cracked open; Ingrid climbs up to it every night.

classification.support_basis: Knowing an open window gives a way into Warwick's house to dose him and reach the chain shirt.

facts.text: Dunk knows Ingrid secretly watches Warwick sleep every night, which she dreads him learning, and he has hinted he might not keep it secret.

classification.support_basis: The secret gives Dunk leverage to keep Ingrid cooperating on the potion scheme.

facts.text: The fauns of the Faun Grove trade their faun wine for sentimental items such as a love letter or a pixie's treasure.

classification.support_basis: More undiluted faun wine could make a stronger sleeping potion if the diluted one fails.
classification.action_basis: The fauns trade wine for sentimental items, and faun wine is the potion's ingredient.

facts.text: Will a potion made from Dunk's heavily diluted faun wine still put Warwick to sleep?

classification.grounding_justification: The wine was established as heavily diluted, clearly raising doubt about the potion's strength.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A single test of the potion would settle it.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly instrumental to the theft plan.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Little beyond testing the potion or asking Ingrid.

facts.text: Does Ingrid really make her potions herself, as she claims, or can't she, as Father William says?

classification.grounding_justification: Ingrid's claim and Father William's contradiction explicitly conflict.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer could reveal a hidden circumstance about Ingrid and where her potions come from.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: It would reveal a secret about Ingrid and change how the party sees her.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be pursued by watching Ingrid or questioning her and Father William.

facts.text: Father William says the dragon can't be killed without the magic sword buried with Sir Brandon in his Barrow Mound; the party could go to the Barrow and retrieve it.
facts.ended_how: used up: Sir Phidipaldi retrieved the sword from Sir Brandon's sarcophagus; the sword is now tracked on thread_3

classification.support_basis: Father William said the sword is required to kill the dragon, so retrieving it was a decisive step.
classification.action_basis: The Barrow's location was known and the party could travel there to retrieve the sword.

facts.text: Father William marked the Barrow Mound's location on Dr. Uriah's map; he says it is about a day's walk away, while the party also heard it is roughly a three-mile walk through the forest.
facts.ended_how: used up: the party reached the Barrow Mound and retrieved the sword

classification.support_basis: The marked map let the party find the Barrow where the sword lay.

facts.text: Will Brother Dirk continue to the Barrow with the party, or go home?
facts.ended_how: answered: Brother Dirk came to the Barrow with the party

classification.grounding_justification: Dirk's hesitation raised whether he would continue.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A simple fact about his choice.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Settled by simply seeing what he does.

facts.text: Is Sir Brandon's magic sword really buried in his Barrow Mound?
facts.ended_how: answered: the sword lay in Sir Brandon's sarcophagus and Sir Phidipaldi took it

classification.grounding_justification: The sword's presence rested on legend and Father William's word.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: One discovery at the tomb would settle it.

facts.text: Dr. Uriah owes Father William penance at the Barrow Mound and a 10 gold donation for the Mound's upkeep.

classification.stake_basis: Father William specifically asked for the donation toward the Mound's upkeep and for Uriah's penance there; no further reliance is established.

facts.text: Why are fairies that used to stay hidden now encroaching and coming out more often, as Ingrid reports?

classification.grounding_justification: Ingrid explicitly reported that formerly hidden fairies are now encroaching, a conspicuous change in their behavior.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal an underlying cause behind a change in fairy behavior across the region.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Learning why the fairies are emerging would explain a broader change in the world and likely reveal a hidden circumstance.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: The question plausibly supports following leads, questioning Ingrid and others, and observing fairy activity.

facts.text: A slow-moving giant living in an oversized cottage of cyclopean rocks in the woods north of Brandonsford captures people to eat; Brother Dirk says the giant meant to cook him in a stew. The giant is now awake and chased the party until he tired.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: The giant captures people to eat them, a specific harm.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Being captured and eaten is death.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Brother Dirk's testimony and the party's own experience of being chased support it.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: The giant is awake and has already captured Dirk and chased the party, but no further movement is established.
classification.preventability_justification: The party knows where the giant lives and that he is slow, so it can avoid the area or confront him, though the means of stopping him are unsettled.

facts.text: A seven-foot undead brown skeleton in rusted armor and a mustachioed death mask, dragging a huge greatsword, has appeared in the doorway of Sir Brandon's tomb as the party prepares to leave. The goblins say it killed many of their kin below, and the slime says it is very mad and roams the lower level.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: It has cut down fleeing goblins with sword wounds and now blocks the tomb doorway where the party stands, so a violent attack on the party is the clear outcome.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: It hacked several goblins to pieces; an attack could kill party members.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: The goblins' and slime's testimony is corroborated by the hacked goblin bodies and by the creature appearing in person.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: It has a pattern of killing intruders and is now physically at the doorway with its greatsword.
classification.preventability_justification: The party can fight, flee or try to parley, and Sir Phidipaldi carries a magical sword and Saint Arthur's favor for the mound, but the outcome is uncertain.

facts.text: Who is the undead swordsman? Is it one of Sir Brandon's companions from the mosaics?

classification.grounding_justification: The goblins claim the killer is one of the mosaic figures. The mosaics show Alfred as a huge man with a greatsword, and the figure that appears matches that, so the identity is conspicuously raised.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal why a companion of Brandon rose as an angry undead guarding the tomb, which is a hidden circumstance.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Learning that a hero's companion became a mad undead would change the party's understanding of the barrow.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: The mosaics, statues, Brother Dirk and the creature itself offer some leads, but a confrontation will likely settle it.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi promised the Free Goblin Society that the party would clear the evil from the Barrow Mound so the goblins can live there free from King Hogboon. In exchange the goblins walk with the party and gift him his 'father's goods'.

classification.stake_basis: The goblins are claiming the mound as the first home of their society, and many of their number have already died below.

facts.text: Under the same bargain, the party must not tell King Hogboon that the Free Goblin Society is living in the Barrow Mound.

classification.stake_basis: The goblins have just left King Hogboon to be free and want to live in the mound out of his reach.

facts.text: The undead greatsword-wielder who has been killing goblins below blocks clearing the evil from the Barrow Mound.

classification.scope_basis: The creature has killed many goblins over time and remains active in the mound. The bargain cannot be fulfilled while it remains.

facts.text: What is making the scratching sounds at the far west end of the Barrow Mound's lower corridor?

classification.grounding_justification: Scratching sounds were heard from an unexplored corridor of a mound the party must clear, which loosely raises the question.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Going to look would settle it.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: It is mainly practical knowledge for clearing the mound.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: It needs only a check of the corridor's end.

facts.text: Do the robes of Saint Arthur, now worn by Dr. Uriah, hold any magic?

classification.grounding_justification: Dr. Uriah explicitly could not test the saint's robes for magic without Ingrid's witch powder, and wearing them had no notable effect, leaving the question open.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Answering it identifies a property of an item.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Learning a saint's robes are magical would be mildly interesting but mainly instrumental.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Settled by a single test with Ingrid's witch powder.

facts.text: Does the jeweled chalice Trout took from Sir Brandon's tomb belong to the church, as Brother Dirk suggests?

classification.grounding_justification: Dirk claimed the chalice was surely a gift to the church and Trout explicitly deferred the matter to be figured out later.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: It mostly settles a claim of ownership, with little hidden truth behind it.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly matters for who keeps a 600-gold item and relations with Dirk's church.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be settled by asking the church or Dirk's superiors.

facts.text: Who does the noblewoman statue holding a stone sword in the Barrow Mound depict?

classification.grounding_justification: The statue guards Brandon's tomb in a hidden room, none of Brandon's companions in the mosaics were women, and Brother Dirk, who knows the tale well, could not identify her.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Her identity would reveal a figure absent from the known tale of Sir Brandon and her role in his burial.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Identifying a woman missing from the legend could change the party's understanding of Brandon's story.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: The mosaics, the church and Brandonsford's lore are plausible sources to question or examine.

facts.text: Whose female voice spoke in the party's heads asking "What makes a true knight?" before the tomb doors opened?

classification.grounding_justification: A telepathic female voice posing a riddle that opened the tomb doors is a conspicuous supernatural anomaly left unexplained.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal what presence or power guards Brandon's tomb and possibly its link to the statue.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Learning who speaks in the tomb would be a revealing supernatural discovery.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: It could be pursued through the statue, the legend and the church's knowledge, though leads are few.
